stem: Of the respondents who prefer online news, what percent are under 35?
explanation: "Of the respondents who prefer online news" means divide by the Online column total, 160. Under 35 and online: 72. $\frac{72}{160} = 0.45 = 45\%$.

choiceExplanations.A: $\frac{72}{300}$ divides by the grand total instead of the Online total.
choiceExplanations.B: $\frac{100}{300}$ is the share of all respondents who are under 35.
choiceExplanations.D: $\frac{160}{300}$ is the share of all respondents who prefer online news.
choiceExplanations.E: $\frac{72}{100}$ is the percent of under-35 respondents who prefer online news: the reverse question.

figure.title: Preferred news source of 300 survey respondents, by age group
figure.notes: Each respondent chose exactly one source.

stem: Complaints of the three most common types together made up what percent of all the complaints?

choiceExplanations.B: 40% is the most common type alone.
choiceExplanations.C: 65% covers only the top two types.

stem: Which of the following statements are supported by the graph? Indicate all such statements.
explanation: The axis starts at 300, so heights are not proportional to the values; read the values: Alton 310, Brook 340, Carver 350, Dell 320. Carver $-$ Alton $= 40$ liters (B). Brook is $\frac{30}{310} \approx 9.7\%$ above Alton (C). Carver is only $\frac{350}{310} \approx 1.13$ times Alton, and Dell is far from double Alton.

choiceExplanations.A: Carver's bar is 5 times as tall as Alton's only because the axis starts at 300: $\frac{350}{310} \approx 1.13$.
choiceExplanations.D: Dell's bar is twice as tall as Alton's, but $320$ is not twice $310$.

figure.title: Average daily water use per household in four towns

stem: Which interval contains the median waiting time?
explanation: With 60 callers, the median is the average of the 30th and 31st times. Running totals: 16 (0–4), 28 (5–9), 37 (10–14). The 30th and 31st callers both fall in 10–14.

choiceExplanations.A: 0–4 holds the most callers (the mode), but only the first 16 in order.
choiceExplanations.B: Only 28 callers are in the first two rows, fewer than the 30 needed.
choiceExplanations.D: 15–19 is the middle of the time range 0 to 29, not the interval holding the middle caller.
choiceExplanations.E: By 20–24, 47 callers are already counted before it begins.

figure.title: Waiting times of 60 callers to a help line
figure.notes: Each waiting time was recorded as a whole number of minutes.

stem: In which month was Store K's revenue per unit sold the greatest?
explanation: Read revenue on the left axis and units on the right axis, then divide. Jan \$150,000 ÷ 3,000 = \$50; Mar \$175,000 ÷ 2,000 = \$87.50; Apr \$125,000 ÷ 1,000 = \$125; May \$75,000 ÷ 1,500 = \$50; Jun \$200,000 ÷ 3,500 ≈ \$57. April is greatest.

choiceExplanations.A: In January the line meets the top of the column, but that says nothing about equal values: \$150,000 ÷ 3,000 = \$50.
choiceExplanations.B: March shows a large gap between column and line, but \$175,000 ÷ 2,000 = \$87.50 < \$125.
choiceExplanations.E: June has the most revenue but also the most units: \$200,000 ÷ 3,500 ≈ \$57.

stem: Which of the following statements must be true? Indicate all such statements.
explanation: Only interval counts are known. The median is in 10–14 (running totals 16, 28, 37), so it is at least 10 (A). Least possible mean: every caller at the low end of the row, $\frac{0(16) + 5(12) + 10(9) + 15(10) + 20(8) + 25(5)}{60} = 9.75$, so the mean is at least 9 (C). Greatest possible mean: add 4 to each, 13.75, so it cannot exceed 14 (B false). No row tells whether anyone waited exactly 12 minutes (D).

choiceExplanations.B: Even if every caller waited the longest time in the row (4, 9, 14, …, 29), the mean would be only 13.75 minutes.
choiceExplanations.D: The row 10–14 holds 9 callers, but their exact times are unknown; none need be 12.
